messages:
maya: Hey team — quick heads up. I found a long-lived JWT for our internal api-proxy embedded in a public Colab notebook (google colab gist). It looks like a user pasted a debug snippet. @sahil @ryan please triage. :eyes:

sahil: Can you paste the snippet or a redacted copy? Which environment does the token map to (dev/staging/prod)?

maya: Pasting redacted snippet below (removed actual token, left header/payload shape):
```
# debug snippet from notebook
import requests
headers = {
  "Authorization": "Bearer eyJhbGciOiJ...<REDACTED>...SflK"
}
resp = requests.get("https://proxy.internal.redwood.ai/health", headers=headers)
print(resp.status_code)
```
This token's kid matches the jwt kid we use for the internal proxy service (likely staging cert) per our local mapping. Found via OSINT scan (public notebook).

ops-bot: [automated detection] Public exposure detected: potential service JWT in public notebook. Alert ID: DET-2026-412. Logged to security detections.

ryan: Maya — assume compromise until proven otherwise. Steps: 1) rotate/invalidate token immediately 2) block any outstanding sessions 3) audit access logs for that token 4) notify affected customers if any usage seen. I can rotate the proxy signing key if needed.

eve: I'll take audit logs and look for any anomalous calls or high-volume hits tied to that kid. Which KMS key signs this? If it's the staging KMS we should be fine, but confirm.

maya: Looks like the token was created by the api-proxy service account using kms key projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/proxy/cryptoKeys/proxy-sign. I see two issuances in the last 30d for that kid at 2026-03-18T03:12Z and 2026-03-22T11:05Z.

sahil: I'll run a quick grep across our public repos and gist history for that kid value pattern and the notebook URL. Also will run `proxyctl revoke-token --kid <kid>` against the internal control plane.

maya: Notebook URL: https://colab.research.google.com/notebook#fileId=1a2b3c-public-notebook

deploy-bot: Triggered rotation job proxy-sign-rotation-2112345678, job id ROT-211234-01, started by ryan.

ryan: I've kicked off key rotation and temporary blocking rule at the edge to refuse tokens with that kid. Expected completion ~10m. Once rotation completes we need to ensure service tokens reissue with new kid and that nothing breaks.

eve: Audit initial findings: 2 requests seen in the last 72h from 54.210.32.11 to the internal proxy using that kid. Both were short-lived health checks; no customer data returned. Will expand window to 30d.

sahil: grep results: found the raw token string copy-pasted in 1 public Colab and 2 forks. I submitted takedown requests to the owners and flagged the notebooks to be made private. Also opened a GitHub takedown ticket.

maya: Action items so far: rotate/invalidate exposed kid (ryan) — in progress; audit logs and scope usage (eve) — in progress; takedown and public remediation (sahil) — in progress; security bulletin draft if customer impact (maya) — pending.

eve: No customer API keys appear to be involved. This was an internal service JWT used for proxy-to-backend. Still running full query: `SELECT * FROM audit.logs WHERE token_kid=\"<kid>\"` (running).

ryan: Rotation finished. Edge block in place. ROT job succeeded. New kid: kid-rot-2026-03-25-01. Please validate services.

sahil: Services report: all internal infra services reissued tokens, CI/CD deployments restarted and healthy. No regression reported in last 15m.

eve: Audit complete: 6 total usages in 90d, 2 of which came after the notebook publish time but all were internal health checks. No read of customer data. Exported log slice to secure drive for post-incident review.

maya: I'm drafting an internal incident note and a short ops email: "Potential exposure of internal proxy JWT in public notebook — rotated and blocked, no customer impact identified, public artifacts takedown in progress, next steps: rotate staging KMS, add detection rule for kid pattern in public notebooks."

ryan: Also recommend: 1) enforce never-commit CI check for tokens in notebooks 2) add a PR hook that scrubs Colab snippets for Authorization headers 3) short-term: reduce token TTL for proxy service and require KMS-based rotation. Assigning owners: sahil -> takedown (due EOD), eve -> audit writeup (due EOD), maya -> comms draft (due EOD), ryan -> follow-up key policy (due 48h).

maya: Filing incident ticket INC-2026-293 and scheduling postmortem. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
